paper.title: Direct Preference Optimization: Your Language Model is Secretly a Reward Model

repo.description: Reference DPO implementation (SFT + DPO trainers, Hydra configs).

claims.text: The DPO loss is the negative log-sigmoid of beta times the difference between the policy-to-reference log-ratios of the preferred and dispreferred completions.
The implicit reward of a completion is beta times the log-ratio of the policy and reference model probabilities.
The default hyperparameters for DPO training are a beta of 0.1, a batch size of 64, and the RMSprop optimizer with a learning rate of 1e-6, which is linearly warmed up from 0 over 150 steps.
claims.notes: config.yaml: RMSprop and warmup_steps 150 match; lr 5e-7 vs 1e-6; batch_size 4 (README passes 64); beta is ??? (required on the CLI).

claims.text: Sequence log-probabilities are the sum of per-token log-probabilities over the completion tokens, ignoring prompt and padding tokens.
The chosen and rejected completions are concatenated into one batch so the policy runs a single forward pass for both.
The single-turn dialogue experiment uses the Anthropic Helpful and Harmless dataset.
The dialogue experiments use a Pythia-2.8B model.
The reference policy is initialised from the SFT model: DPO training loads the SFT checkpoint into both the policy and the reference model.
The reference model is kept frozen and evaluated without gradients during DPO training.
